rows.what: A TRUNCATED BACKLOG ID — IN THE RECEIPT ITSELF, AND THE SECOND TIME THIS SESSION. The MI-331 decision row cited the MI-331 arbitration-fanout backlog row by a PREFIX, dropping its `-BECAUSE-APPLY-ROUNDS-DROPS-THE-GEOMETRY-ITS-OWN-READER-VALIDATES` tail. check_backlog_refs.py failed the `guards` job on head f16915204: a reference that resolves to NOTHING reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. I had already made this exact mistake earlier the same session on #12580 and fixed it there — so this is a RECURRENCE, and that it recurred inside the artifact whose job is to record such things is the finding. ⚠️ AND THE FIRST FIX FAILED THE SAME GUARD AGAIN, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF: I expanded the id, then WROTE THE TRUNCATED FORM A SECOND TIME in this very error row while describing the mistake — and abbreviated four MORE ids with a trailing `...` in the new backlog row's similarity-check note. The guard reads a PREFIX, so quoting a shortened id to talk ABOUT shortened ids re-introduces the defect. Five refusals on the second run, from one root.
rows.correction: Expanded every id to its full form — the four neighbours in the backlog row and the one in this receipt — and stopped quoting truncated ids in prose at all: this row now names the offending row by description rather than by a prefix. Fix-forward is valid here because check_backlog_refs grades the DIFF against origin/main, unlike check_manager_scope and check_pr_landing which grade the COMMIT RANGE and need history rewritten. ⚠️ THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT CARELESSNESS AND A THIRD RESOLUTION TO BE CAREFUL WOULD NOT HOLD — it has now failed twice in one session: these ids run past 100 characters and get hand-quoted into prose, where abbreviating them is the natural thing to do. `scripts/ops/session_receipt.py --resolve-id` already exists to expand a prefix to its full form and I did not use it; using it, and running check_backlog_refs BEFORE pushing rather than after CI says so, is the mechanism.
